title: Poland's Twin Fiscal Battles: Tax Reform and Fuel Relief Test Government's… · 22 Aug
keywords: Poland, tax reform, budget deficit, fiscal policy, fuel prices, inflation, cost of living, VAT cut, NBP, EU fiscal framework, Central Europe, Warsaw, corporate tax, household relief
notes: Poland's government is pushing a sweeping tax overhaul aimed at easing burdens on middle-income households while raising levies on large corporations and top earners, even as it simultaneously reintroduces fuel-price relief measures to contain summer cost-of-living pressures. The dual initiatives come against a backdrop of sharply deteriorating public finances, with the budget deficit reaching 141 billion zlotys after just seven months of 2026. Together, the moves expose the central contradiction facing Warsaw: how to promise households relief while acknowledging the state is running short of fiscal room.
